The first release of Axolotl, a null-safe language that translates to readable Java 21.

## Downloads

- `axl-0.1.0.zip`: the command line compiler. Unzip it and put `bin` on your `PATH`; it needs Java 21.
- `axolotl-0.1.0.vsix`: the VS Code extension: `code --install-extension axolotl-0.1.0.vsix`.
- `axl-intellij-0.1.0.zip`: the IntelliJ IDEA plugin: *Settings | Plugins | Install Plugin from Disk*.

The Gradle and Maven plugins are not published to a public repository yet; build them with
`./gradlew publishToMavenLocal` as described in the [installation guide](https://github.com/sora-vuv/axolotl-lang/blob/v0.1.0/docs/install.md).

## What is in it

- Values that may be null are typed with `?` and checked by the compiler, javac, Error Prone and NullAway.
- `try` and `attempt` work with `Result` values, and pipes (`|>`) turn into streams.
- `when` with type tests and constants, `data class`, `sealed interface`, `enum`, `class` and `for` loops.
- Errors are reported at `.axl` lines and columns, in Axolotl terms; stack traces and debuggers show `.axl` lines.
- Gradle and Maven plugins, a language server, and plugins for VS Code and IntelliJ IDEA.
- The compiler is written in Axolotl itself.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/sora-vuv/axolotl-lang/blob/v0.1.0/CHANGELOG.md) for details.

## Known limitations

- An `Int?` and a `Long?` branch cannot be mixed in one value, and `Int? ?: 0L` is rejected.
- `var x = when` with lambdas in its branches needs a written type.
- Error Prone in Maven needs `.mvn/jvm.config`, and Gradle compiles in a forked JVM.
